clue.text: Restless person taking false silver back and forth

indicators.note: back tells us the two pieces before it, false and silver, are turned round as one run

parts.note: false means bad, as in a bad coin
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
forth means out, as in going forth

explanation.surface: A fidgety soul carries forged silver to and fro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns BAD + AG together into GADAB; 'and' is a link, and 'back and forth' is not the phrase it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gads about, flitting from one social outing to the next, is never settled.

clue.text: Glorious opening to stir up birds

indicators.note: opening points to the first letter of the word Glorious

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up

explanation.surface: The Glorious Twelfth begins and the shooting party flushes out game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious Twelfth, 12 August, opens the British grouse-shooting season.
explanation.definitionFit: These game birds are moorland fowl shot for sport; the word serves as its own plural.

clue.text: Animals in Oz avoid battle-axes

parts.note: to duck a question is to avoid it
a bill is a medieval halberd, a blade on a long pole

explanation.surface: Australian creatures dodge shrewish old women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battle-axes' suggests formidable women; here it is the weapon, the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Platypuses, native to Australia, are nicknamed for their flat, beak-like snouts.

clue.text: Novelist yielding stone to graduate in game

parts.note: beryl is a gemstone
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A writer turns a gem over to a graduate at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but simply supplies its own two letters; Beryl Bainbridge was a Booker-shortlisted English novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The English author of The Bottle Factory Outing wrote fiction.

clue.text: Vain tennis player interrupting us…

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the player goes inside the other word

parts.note: Monica Seles was a champion tennis player

explanation.surface: A tennis star butts in on our conversation to no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain in the sense of futile: achieving nothing, of no avail.

clue.text: Song in honour of Suleyman the Magnificent

indicators.note: of here means made from part of, so the letters lie within the Sultan's title that follows

explanation.surface: A hymn composed to praise the great Ottoman sultan.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'suleymAN THE Magnificent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A national or celebratory song is written to praise a country, cause or person.

clue.text: … yet lacking status

parts.note: lacking means not with, without
standing means status or rank

explanation.surface: It continues the previous clue: a vain player, though without rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this to 4 down so the two read as one sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean nevertheless or in spite of that.

clue.text: Empty house next to craft centre

indicators.note: empty means hollowed out, leaving only the first and last letters of house

parts.note: craft means art or skill

explanation.surface: A vacant house beside a craft centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft centre' looks like one phrase; centre is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or middle of something is its innermost part.

clue.text: Woman in charge of military intelligence -a sign of importance

parts.note: a stress mark shows emphasis, signalling which syllable matters

explanation.surface: A woman commanding army spies shows her importance.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who heads a household or school, or has authority over servants.

clue.text: About the fourth of July beasts see stars

parts.note: c, circa, means about

indicators.note: fourth of picks the fourth letter of July

parts.note: gnus are wildebeest

explanation.surface: Around Independence Day, animals see stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see stars' suggests being dazed; 'see' is a link and 'stars' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swan is a northern constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Award for Cliff after photo finish

indicators.note: after places the cliff word behind the photo's closing letter
finish points to the closing letter of the word photo

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff

explanation.surface: A prize for Cliff Richard once the photo-finish result is in.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff looks like the singer Cliff Richard; it is a common noun, a scar or crag.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy's statuette is the film industry's best-known prize.

clue.text: People say pay isn't negotiable

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: something negotiable is open to being reworked, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Workers protest that their wages are fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People say' reads as hearsay; 'say' gives the abbreviation for 'for example', and 'negotiable' signals the reshuffle of the remaining words.
explanation.definitionFit: The inhabitants of a North African nation form a people.

clue.text: Officer in naval craft has to change direction

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a naval vessel
to change is to alter
N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: An officer aboard a navy vessel must alter course.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior army officer below captain rank holds this title.

clue.text: Section of train terminating at Bury

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a railway service ends at the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'at Bury' as the definition, but 'at' is a link word; 'Bury' alone means the answer. Bury is a town near Manchester, which is what the surface pretends.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body is to place it in a grave, a formal burial.

clue.text: Poor laws binding for ever and ever

indicators.note: binding means wrapping round, so the scrambled letters enclose the other piece
poor suggests something badly made, so these letters come out rearranged

parts.note: ay or aye is an old word for ever, as in for ever and aye

explanation.surface: Bad legislation shackles us in perpetuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' signals the reshuffle of laws, and 'binding' wraps the result round the old word for ever; 'for ever and ever' looks like one phrase but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at all times, perpetually, continues without end.

clue.text: Examinations for swimming groups

explanation.surface: Tests for groups learning to swim.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford University the final examinations are called Schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford's degree finals bear this name, and fish swimming together form shoals or these.

clue.text: Art song is work for play ers

indicators.note: work means rework or knead, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A song is a piece written for performers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who play church instruments are performers.

clue.text: Handle to seize when reversing canal cruiser

indicators.note: when reversing means both pieces are read backwards as one run

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name
to grab is to seize

explanation.surface: A grip to grab when backing a boat along the canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when reversing' turns NAMEGRAB into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who works on or steers a narrow freight boat travels canals.

clue.text: Want small enclosure in Lincoln?

indicators.note: in places the small enclosure inside the president's name

parts.note: Abe was the short name of US President Abraham Lincoln
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosure, as in a letter

explanation.surface: Is there a lack of tiny pens in the city of Lincoln?
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln seems to be the English cathedral city; it is the president.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack: a shortage or nonexistence of something.

clue.text: Unmask former spouse with model

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
to model is to pose

explanation.surface: Reveal a previous husband with a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose is to reveal the truth or show someone up.

clue.text: Cook got pea soup

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The chef has made pea soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick broth, from the French word for a pot-cooked dish.

clue.text: Adriatic resort importing border flower

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the border goes inside the resort

parts.note: Pula is a Croatian resort on the Adriatic
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A seaside town brings in a flower for its borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border flower' reads as a garden plant; border is the RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose belongs to this genus of spring-blooming plants.

clue.text: Going up, go in tree or shrub

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, backwards
in places the attempt inside the tree

parts.note: an elm is a tree
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: Climbing, have a go at the tree or bush.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Going up' reverses the whole tree-with-attempt combination, read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen bush with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Little lad taken aback by Georgia and Eva

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: taken aback reads as surprised but here signals the name is turned backwards

parts.note: Rob is a short form of the boy's name Robert

explanation.surface: A small boy is startled by Georgia and Eva.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva was one of the Hungarian-born sisters, actresses famous in Hollywood.

clue.text: High-ranking lady, example, embraced tramp

indicators.note: embraced means held within, so the example goes inside the tramp

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant
eg, for example

explanation.surface: A grand lady was hugged by a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim woman of high rank in South Asia bears this title.

clue.text: Retreating soldier is sheltered by flower-girl-it's so touching!

definitions.note: an exclamation standing for the noun: the quality of being so touching

indicators.note: is sheltered by puts the turned soldier within the flower and girl pieces

parts.note: a flower in crosswords is a river, something that flows; the Po is Italy's river
Nancy is a girl's name

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the soldier's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A deserter hides with a flower seller, and it moves us all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower-girl' reads as a seller of flowers; split it into flower (a river, the Italian one) and a girl's name. 'Retreating' turns the soldier round.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignancy is the quality of stirring sadness or tender emotion.

clue.text: Smug Idaho resort or port

indicators.note: read as re-sort: sort the letters again, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smug holiday spot in Idaho, or else a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a holiday place but is re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia's capital is a harbour city on the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Implant required by fashionable group

parts.note: in means fashionable
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Trendy people demand a transplant.
explanation.definitionFit: To inset is to put in or embed one thing within another.

clue.text: Issue anaesthetic?

explanation.surface: Is a numbing drug the subject?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as numb-er, something that numbs; the question mark flags the made-up sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine issue is identified by its sequence count, and a drug that deadens feeling would be a numb-er.

clue.text: Audible feature of Snickers or Bounty?

indicators.note: audible says the words are heard spoken, so the spelling follows their sound

parts.note: the brand name Snickers begins with a large letter S

explanation.surface: What can be heard in a Snickers or Bounty chocolate bar?
explanation.walkthrough: Snickers and Bounty are chocolate bars; Bounty is really the definition, generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generosity in giving, as a bounty is a generous gift.
